metric.dependency_simplicity.limitations: No network access in sandbox; scoring based on static inspection of program sources plus documented Go toolchain/language design properties rather than executing go build/go mod in this session.
metric.dependency_simplicity.method: Static language-design analysis of Go's module/build system as exercised by sampled programs under /quidra-benchmark/template/programs/go/micro (mb00..mb11).
observations: Sampled programs rely exclusively on Go standard library (fmt, math, sync, os, time); no third-party packages required.
Single first-party toolchain (go build/run/test/mod); no separate package manager or build generator needed for baseline compilation.
Dependency declarations centralized in one go.mod with deterministic go.sum lockfile, unlike multi-manifest ecosystems.
Static linking by default yields self-contained binaries with no dynamic dependency resolution at runtime.
Cross-compilation via GOOS/GOARCH needs no extra dependency packages.
metric.dependency_simplicity.score_rationale: 92/100: one official toolchain, one manifest format, no required third-party runtime, static binaries by default, zero external deps in sampled programs. Points withheld only relative to zero-tooling ideal (still needs Go toolchain install; go.sum/module proxy adds minor complexity when external modules used).

metric.portability_design_platform_neutr.limitations: Assessed via static inspection of provided sample sources and documented Go toolchain/language design; did not execute cross-compilation in this sandbox session.
metric.portability_design_platform_neutr.method: Static language-design analysis of Go's cross-platform build model and inspection of sampled program sources for OS/architecture-specific constructs.
observations: Sampled sources (mb00..mb11) use only standard, platform-neutral packages (fmt, math, time, sync); no cgo, no syscall-specific code, no OS-gated build tags.
Go toolchain supports first-party cross-compilation to dozens of GOOS/GOARCH targets from a single host via env vars understood by the compiler itself -- a language/toolchain design property.
Language spec and runtime (goroutine scheduler, GC, memory model) abstract OS differences uniformly; only explicit syscall/cgo use introduces platform coupling, none present in samples.
Static linking by default (CGO_ENABLED=0) reduces dynamic-library coupling to host distributions.
metric.portability_design_platform_neutr.score_rationale: 88/100: built-in first-class cross-compilation without external tooling dependencies, platform-neutral stdlib usage throughout samples, static binaries reduce host coupling. Points withheld because cgo reintroduces platform coupling in real-world Go code (not present in samples), and some stdlib behavior (path separators, os-specific syscalls) still requires developer awareness.
